item.text:
**3B.3 Research Note**

Overall, I found no reliable evidence that Srettha personally incited hatred, dehumanization, revenge, or violence against opponents, minorities, migrants, journalists, or civil society in 2024. The clearest evidence is the opposite: official rights-forward rhetoric and inclusive diplomatic language. The negative side is indirect, showing a hostile rights environment under his government, but not direct personal incitement.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Prime Minister delivers statement at 3rd Summit for Democracy, highlighting Thailand’s commitment to democracy, rule of law, and human rights at home and abroad | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-03-20 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/summit-for-democracy-3-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Srettha publicly tied his government to democracy, rule of law, and human rights. That is direct evidence against personal incitement or dehumanizing rhetoric. | 3B.3 |
| Positive | Statement by H.E. Mr. Srettha Thavisin Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand at the General Debate of the 78th Session of the United Nations General Assembly | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2023-09-19, but used as background into 2024 posture | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/statement-unga-gd-78-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | He framed policy around equality, justice, the vulnerable, and the marginalized, and said the law should apply fairly to everyone. This is inclusive rhetoric rather than scapegoating. | 3B.3 |
| Positive | Joint Statement by the Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand and the Prime Minister of New Zealand | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-04-17 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/js170424-2?menu=5d5bd3da15e39c306002aafa&page=5d5bd3da15e39c306002aaf9 | The joint statement emphasized democratic values, human rights, good governance, rule of law, and multilateralism. This is consistent with non-incendiary leadership language. | 3B.3 |
| Positive | Statement by Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs at the High-level Segment during the 55th Session of the Human Rights Council | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-02-28 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/statement-vfm-280224?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c3060006848 | Thailand said it promotes human rights for all, humanitarian assistance to all in need, dialogue, reconciliation, and inclusive societies. This directly cuts against hatred or scapegoating. | 3B.3 |
| Negative / indirect | World Report 2025: Thailand | Human Rights Watch | 2025-01-xx, covering events of 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/thailand | HRW says the 2024 government continued restrictions on expression and assembly and prosecutions of critics of the monarchy. This is evidence of a repressive environment, but it is not itself proof that Srettha personally incited hatred or violence. | 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative / indirect | Thailand: New Government Slow to Protect Rights | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/thailand-new-government-slow-protect-rights | HRW urged Srettha to end politically motivated prosecutions and drop charges against peaceful protesters and those accused of insulting the monarchy. This supports a negative reading of tolerance for repression, but not direct personal incitement. | 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative / indirect | Thailand: ‘Swap Mart’ Targets Foreign Dissidents, Refugees | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-15 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/15/thailand-swap-mart-targets-foreign-dissidents-refugees | HRW said Thai authorities had cooperated in transnational repression against dissidents and refugees. That is relevant to tolerating abuse of critics and migrants, but the article does not show Srettha himself inciting such conduct. | 3B.3, 3B.2 |

**Search gap**
I did not find a 2024 source showing Srettha personally used hate speech, dehumanization, revenge rhetoric, or ethnic/religious scapegoating. The strongest negative evidence is structural: ongoing prosecutions, repression of critics, and transnational repression concerns under Thai authorities. That supports a “tolerated hostile environment” reading, not a direct-incitement finding.
